item.title: Alibaba Fined €550 Million for Illegal Sales in Biggest DSA Case
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s e-commerce service was fined €550 million ($629 million) by the European Union for selling illegal products in the largest penalty under the bloc’s content moderation rulebook.

item.title: SBI Funds Pays Razor-Thin Banker Fees on Top India IPO of 2026
item.description: The nine investment banks that manage SBI Funds Management Ltd.‘s initial public offering, India‘s first billion-dollar debut this year, will receive one of the worst payouts on a large debut in the country.

item.description: The popular Magnificent Seven stocks moniker is “no longer relevant” in assessing how to play the US artificial intelligence trade, according to Citigroup Inc. strategists.

item.description: Moonshot AI’s surprise release of a new artificial intelligence model has sent a jolt through markets, forcing investors to reassess some of the biggest assumptions behind the global tech rally.

item.title: Euro-Area Firms Faced Rising Interest Rates in Second Quarter
item.description: Euro-area firms were confronted with higher interest rates and tighter lending conditions in the second quarter when the Iran war clouded the region’s economic outlook, according to a survey published by the European Central Bank.

item.title: US Gasoline Prices Surpass $4 a Gallon for First Time in a Month
item.description: US gasoline prices climbed back over the $4-a-gallon mark at the pump as the conflict in the Middle East escalated, threatening to exacerbate a global crunch for transportation fuels and stoke inflation.

item.title: Hong Kong Stock-Listing Boom Rumbles Toward Six-Year High
item.description: A summer of mega deals is supercharging Hong Kong’s boom for stock-market debuts, with the city poised to notch a six-year high for proceeds barely more than halfway through 2026.

item.title: AI Is ‘New Engine’ Keeping Chinese Economy From Harder Landing
item.description: A global rush to build out artificial intelligence infrastructure has turned the technology into a key pocket of growth in China’s economy during one of its weakest stretches in years.

item.title: Rising Demand for Hedges Hints at Volatility Ahead: Taking Stock
item.description: The momentum trade carried along by the equity rally is faltering, while optimistic earnings expectations are under intense scrutiny, two of the signs pointing to a volatile summer.

item.title: Segro Rejects Fresh £13.5 Billion Cash and Share Prologis Offer
item.description: Segro Plc has rejected the latest proposal from Prologis Inc. that offered about £13.5 billion for the UK warehouse landlord.

item.title: China Is Exporting 20% Fewer Magnets to US Despite Trade Truce
item.description: China’s shipments of rare-earth magnets to the US remain well below pre-trade war levels despite last year’s truce, underscoring concerns in the Trump administration about Beijing’s adherence to that agreement.

item.title: Octopus-Backed MOPO Partners Nigeria in $75 Million Battery Plan
item.description: MOPO, an Africa-focused battery rental company backed by Octopus Energy Group Ltd., said it’s signed an agreement with Nigeria to facilitate a $75 million expansion of its activities in Africa’s most populous nation.

item.title: Prysmian Signs $6.3 Billion Molex Deal for Data-Center Gear
item.description: Prysmian SpA signed a deal worth as much €5.5 billion ($6.3 billion) with Koch Inc.’s Molex to supply optical cables to data centers, tapping into the surge in investment in artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Moonshot’s Kimi K3 May Be More About Memory Than Compute
item.description: When DeepSeek’s R1 debuted in early 2025, almost $600 billion was wiped out from Nvidia Corp.’s market value in a single day on fears that artificial intelligence would require less computing power than previously expected. Moonshot AI’s release of Kimi K3 on Friday triggered a similar reaction, helping push semiconductor stocks sharply lower.

item.title: China Solar Stocks Rise After Beijing Issues Consumption Tax
item.description: Shares of most Chinese solar and major battery makers rose on Monday after Beijing unveiled a consumption tax on solar cells and lithium batteries, raising hopes it will hasten industry consolidation, particularly in the oversupplied solar sector.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Mixed as Investors Weigh Iran Tensions
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies were mixed as investors weighed rising tensions between the US and Iran, as well as a technology-led selloff that rattled global markets last week.

item.title: Blackstone Agrees to Invest in Korean Robotics Supplier Futronic
item.description: Blackstone Inc. has agreed to invest in Futronic, a South Korean supplier of high-precision actuators used in industrial robotics and the automotive sector.

item.title: Palm Climbs to Near One-Month High as Iran Conflict Boosts Crude
item.description: Palm oil rose to the highest in nearly a month, tracking renewed strength in crude and other vegetable oil prices as the US and Iran exchanged escalating military strikes.

item.title: RBI Intervenes to Support Rupee as Currency Nears Record Low
item.description: India’s central bank stepped into the foreign exchange markets to support the rupee after the currency weakened toward a record low as a renewed surge in crude prices weighed on sentiment.

item.title: Britain’s Middle Class Feels the Strain as Burnham Vows to Help
item.description: Britain’s middle class is showing signs of buckling under financial pressure, with incoming prime minister Andy Burnham considering a wave of interventions to ease the cost of living.

item.title: Key China Copper Gauge Rallies to $100 After Tax Crackdown
item.description: A closely-watched gauge of China’s copper market has risen to the highest in more than a year, as a tax shake-up in the metal’s biggest market spurs a shortage of scrap and boosts demand for imports.

item.title: AI Pioneer Kai-Fu Lee’s Startup Targets Hong Kong IPO Next Year
item.description: 01.ai, the Chinese AI startup founded by computer scientist Kai-Fu Lee, is pushing ahead with plans to raise funds before an initial public offering in 2027.

item.title: Hedge Funds Dial Up Bearish Kiwi Bets to Record on Oil Rebound
item.description: Leveraged funds have taken their short positions on the New Zealand dollar to a record high, betting that a recent rebound in global oil prices may exacerbate domestic economic pressures.

item.description: Managements sounded fairly confident that credit demand will hold up.
